Lipik Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lipik, Croatia

Not demolished. Lipik, already a well-known balneological resort under the Russian Empire, drew Croatian families after liberation from nearly 150 years of Turkish rule in 1691, thanks to its distinctive healing iodine waters. Jews settled in Lipik in the 19th century, and this cemetery — part of the main municipal cemetery — was established around the same time; by 1931, 47 Jews lived among the town's 1,200 residents. During WWII, all 41 of Lipik's Jews were sent to concentration camps, where they died; no Jews remained in the town afterward.
